executive_summary: EUR/CHF closed at 0.92064 on 30 October 2026. The pair is quoted in francs per euro, so a rising pair means a stronger euro. It is down 1.46% over one month and 1.31% over three months, up 0.59% over six months and down 0.40% over a year. Measured from the 30 September close of 0.94696, October's fall was 2.78%, the sharpest monthly drop the pair has had in years. The main story is a euro-specific sovereign and energy shock. The OAT-Bund spread hit a 15-year high, Dutch TTF gas reached EUR 100/MWh, and the SNB on 22 October confirmed it no longer sees an 'increased willingness to intervene' as necessary. That loosens the brake on franc strength just as haven demand returned. The two currency views disagree here. The euro view is bearish mostly against the dollar and treats this cross as the euro's best carry trade. The franc view is Neutral overall but bullish against the euro on haven and fiscal grounds. Once the dollar-driven parts of each view are taken out, what remains is the sovereign and external contrast between France and Switzerland. Our tactical stance is Neutral, conviction 2 (score -0.083): over four weeks a stable 250bp carry offsets a cluster of French and energy risks. Our strategic stance is Bearish, conviction 2 (score -0.317), with a three-month base case of 0.9080. The caveat is that carry and the SNB cap the payoff. Futures roll the euro at an annualised 293bp discount, so a short pays about 22 pips a month. The SNB has shown in 2026 that it will lean against a rapid franc rally near 0.90. The edge is a call on direction against a bank consensus near 0.934, not a large gap to the forward.

market_context.valuation_assessment: On long-run PPP the franc is very expensive. World Bank conversion factors put fair EUR/CHF near 1.3109, a franc premium of about 42%. That gap has persisted for decades and has never closed within a quarter. Real exchange rates on recent history point the other way. The BIS real effective rate for the franc was 98.37 in September, the lowest of 33 monthly readings since January 2024 and 4.6 points lower over a year. The euro's was 103.27, at the 67th percentile of the same window, because euro-area inflation of 3.8% has outrun its partners. What the current level prices is a franc that has already shed the competitiveness premium of 2024–25, and a euro whose real rate has been flattered by inflation rather than earned. Valuation therefore gives no short-horizon signal, but it removes the 'franc too expensive' argument that would normally cap the Swiss surplus. Spot sits at the 44th percentile of the intraday 52-week range (42nd on closing prices, range 0.90152–0.94701), so October gave back the August–September rally and returned the pair to the middle of the year's range.

market_context.recent_regime: From June to September the pair traded as a carry cross. The SNB held at zero while the ECB hiked twice, and the pair climbed from the 0.91 May lows to 0.947 in September. October broke that regime. Saxo's John Hardy recorded a one-session fall from roughly 0.9460 to 0.9325 on 1 October as French yields jumped, and the pair then stepped lower in three waves (1–2, 15–16 and 22 October) as the OAT-Bund spread made new highs. The SNB's softer intervention wording, which replaced 'increased willingness to intervene' with 'also willing to be active in the foreign exchange market as necessary', removed the alert level that had supported the pair in the spring. The dominant narrative is now EUR/CHF as the cleanest market for hedging French risk.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: Policy carry is +250bp a year for a euro holder (ECB deposit 2.50% minus SNB 0%), rising to 275bp if the ECB hikes on 17 December. Listed futures observed 29 October roll the euro at an annualised 293.3bp discount against the franc, which is the rate differential plus cross-currency basis (they cannot be separated); a long EUR/CHF position earns that roll and a short pays it, so the policy carry of +250bp is used as the headline long-side figure. Carry-to-vol is 0.49 on policy carry, 0.58 on the roll and about 0.42 against the corrected volatility of about 6.0%. Forwards discount franc appreciation of about 2.9% a year. The carry regime has been reliable only while euro-area sovereign stress is contained. October's 2.78% fall wiped out more than a year of policy carry in a month, which is how carry behaves in this pair: a steady trickle in calm markets, reversed abruptly by haven episodes. A carry-to-vol of about 0.5 is respectable for G10, but in this pair that figure sits on a fat left tail.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The policy gap is 250bp in the euro's favour. The ECB deposit rate is 2.50% after hikes in June and September and a unanimous hold on 29 October. The SNB policy rate has been 0% since June 2025 and was held on 24 September. Long-end yields agree: the 10-year Bund closed at 3.32-3.40% on 30 October, depending on the series, against 0.47% for the Swiss Confederation 10-year. That is a gap of roughly 285-293bp, close to the 288bp gap between the September monthly averages of 3.47% and 0.59%. Listed futures observed on 29 October roll the euro at an annualised 293bp discount to the franc. That is about 43bp more than the policy gap, a mix of expected ECB-over-SNB tightening and cross-currency basis. Neither central bank decides inside the four-week horizon: the SNB's quarterly assessment is on 10 December and the ECB's projection meeting is on 17 December. Until then the gap can only move through repricing on the 3 November Swiss CPI and the 4 November euro-area HICP flash, and both are expected in line. The carry is stable, sizeable relative to the pair's volatility, and nothing scheduled can compress it before mid-December, so the rate channel leans mildly towards a rising pair.

tactical.what_is_priced: The forward already discounts the 250bp carry plus about 43bp more, in line with a December ECB hike priced above 80% and an SNB on hold. With no decision before 10 December, the four-week edge is that carry keeps accruing while nothing scheduled can narrow the gap.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months, two scheduled decisions settle whether the gap widens to 275bp or stops there. The SNB assessment on 10 December brings a new conditional inflation forecast, and the ECB meeting on 17 December comes with staff projections. The widening is largely priced already: a December ECB hike is above 80% and about 75bp of further ECB tightening is priced in total. The SNB curve, by contrast, prices a hold well into 2027; the Swiss 2-year eased to 0.18% on 30 October from 0.263% a month earlier. Both dossiers see the risk to that pricing pointing towards a narrower gap than the curve implies. The euro view puts the ECB terminal rate at 3.00% rather than about 3.25%, and Lagarde's announced departure in early 2027 raises the odds of an early pause. The franc view gives a 30% chance to an SNB hike by March 2027, which the curve barely prices; Bloomberg Economics flags March 2027 as a possible first move in a high-oil case. Against that, the euro still carries 250-275bp across the horizon, about 0.7% over three months at the futures roll, and a falling pair has to overcome that before it pays. Carry favours a rising pair, the direction of repricing risk favours a falling one, and the 17 December projections are where that gets settled.

carry_analysis.reference: See bilateral_carry_analysis: policy carry 250bp a year (ECB deposit 2.50% minus SNB 0%; 275bp if the ECB hikes in December); futures roll -293.3bp annualised for the euro against the franc (interest differential plus cross-currency basis, observed 29 October 2026).
carry_analysis.breakeven_move: Policy carry is worth about 230 pips a year at the 30 October spot, about 19 pips a month and 58 pips over three months; at the 293bp futures roll about 22 pips a month and 67 pips over three months. The pair has to fall by that much before a short covers its carry.
carry_analysis.note: Carry-to-vol 0.49 is 250bp policy carry divided by the 5.085% estimated 3-month implied volatility; about 0.58 on the 293bp futures roll. The 5.085% is an estimate, not a quote: EUR/CHF has no listed option, so it is built from CME-listed euro and Swiss franc options with the cross-rate variance identity and a realised correlation of 0.685, measured at 98.7 days and observed 29 October 2026. Against direct Eurex quotes on 21 August it understated EUR/CHF volatility by 17.8%, so treat it as a floor; the true ratio is probably somewhat lower (about 0.42). The futures roll of -293.3bp is the annualised premium between two listed futures; it is the interest differential plus cross-currency basis, which cannot be separated, so it is not reported as the policy gap. Carry favours a euro holder by 250bp against the lowest policy rate in G10, but its efficiency depends on the franc's haven role staying dormant: in a euro-specific sovereign shock haven flows can overwhelm several months of carry, so carry has been reliable only while euro-area stress is contained.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation gap is wide. Euro-area HICP was 3.8% in September with core at 2.5%; Swiss CPI was 1.0% with core at 0.5%. That is 280bp on headline and 200bp on core. Real policy rates are much closer than the nominal gap suggests: the ECB's 2.50% less 3.8% inflation is about -1.3%, and the SNB's 0% less 1.0% is about -1.0%, so on headline terms the franc carries the marginally higher real rate. Both economies are slowing from different starting points. Euro-area Q3 GDP rose 0.4% q/q, but France contracted 0.1%, Germany grew only 0.2%, and the October composite PMI fell to 51.9 from 53.1. Swiss Q2 GDP rose 1.5% q/q on a sport-adjusted basis, mostly from pharmaceuticals, and the KOF barometer slipped to 107.6 from 109.1. The two releases inside the horizon, Swiss CPI on 3 November and the euro-area flash on 4 November (consensus 3.9%), are both expected in line. The pair is more sensitive to the Swiss print because almost no SNB tightening is priced: a reading at 1.2% or higher would reprice the SNB, while a euro-area surprise mostly moves a December ECB hike that is already priced. With no expected surprise on either side, the factor is Neutral.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the mix turns against the euro relative to the franc. Euro-area inflation is cost-push. Wages are tracking 2.5-2.8% against 3.8% headline inflation, a real-income squeeze of about one percentage point. Bank lending has slowed and credit standards tightened in Q3, and UBS sees headline HICP peaking at 4.1% in January 2027. That combination squeezes growth rather than attracting capital. Swiss inflation, by contrast, is drifting up from the lowest base in G10: the SNB's conditional forecast is 0.7% for 2026 and 0.8% for 2027 at a 0% rate. Energy is a much smaller share of the Swiss CPI basket, and SECO raised its 2026 growth forecast to 1.7%. In Switzerland, rising inflation is the route to SNB normalisation, the only way the carry gap narrows from the Swiss side. In the euro area, rising inflation mostly erodes real incomes against an ECB terminal that is already priced. The checkpoints are the SNB's new conditional forecast on 10 December and the ECB staff projections on 17 December. Both legs point to a falling pair.

Strategically Bearish because the euro's real-income squeeze and the franc's slow inflation drift both work against the pair over quarters, with the 10 and 17 December forecast rounds as checkpoints.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Tactical weight raised from the 0.10 default. In the current regime EUR/CHF is the main market for hedging euro-area sovereign stress, so risk sentiment transmits more directly into this pair than the moderate-sensitivity default assumes. Strategic weight is the default.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: EUR/CHF is normally only moderately risk-sensitive. The current stress, though, is euro-specific and sovereign, which is the setting where the franc's haven role works most directly against the euro. The OAT-Bund spread hit a 15-year high on 22-23 October and was about 155bp on 29 October, against 78bp a year earlier. The French 10-year reached 5.14% on 23 October, its highest since 2002. Euro high-yield spreads widened to 3.48% on 29 October from 2.94% a month earlier, while the VIX closed at 17.2, so this is regional stress rather than a global de-risking. Market commentary in the last days of October tied the franc's strength explicitly to French bond pressure. The counter-argument is real: IC Markets noted on 2 November that the 0% SNB rate and fading haven concerns limit franc appreciation, and Rabobank describes the franc as caught between funding and haven roles. Inside four weeks, though, the dated risks are skewed against the euro: the French revenue vote on 3 November, the whole-budget vote on 17 November, and the window for a US strike on Iran that opens after the 3 November midterms.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the risk channel is genuinely two-sided for this pair. A settlement of the US-Iran conflict would cut the energy premium and probably narrow French spreads, which would favour the euro. Equities are strong, US credit spreads are tight, and gold, which tends to move with the franc, fell about 7% in October; all three take some shine off the haven case. Rabobank notes that the franc's haven appeal faded after the SNB intervened in March and that a zero policy rate pushes it towards a funding role. Against that, escalation in the Gulf after the midterms, a French government collapse, or a broader equity correction would revive the haven bid, and the French presidential race keeps a euro-specific risk premium alive into 2027. Settlement-led and escalation-led outcomes look roughly equally likely over the horizon, so the factor gives no strategic signal.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Speculators are short both legs, which mutes the signal for the cross. In the week to 27 October, leveraged funds were net short 71,574 euro contracts, the most short since May, and the legacy non-commercial net short reached 143,900. Leveraged funds were also net short 17,502 franc contracts, again the most short in the window. Asset managers are the least long euros and the least short francs of the same period, so real money has been moving towards the franc on both legs. In notional terms the euro short is far larger, about USD 10bn against USD 2.65bn. It is also beyond the level that has marked past euro extremes, whereas the franc short is still below the roughly 30,000-contract scale that has preceded franc squeezes. Most of the euro short is held against the dollar, though, so a euro squeeze would show up mainly in EUR/USD. The official sector is quiet: SNB sight deposits held at CHF 435.36bn in the week to 16 October, showing no intervention against October's franc strength. Crowding on both sides cancels for the cross, so the factor is Neutral.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months, real-money flows matter more than speculative crowding, and they pull in both directions for this cross. Asset managers are still net long 173,249 euro contracts, about 117,000 below their window peak, so there is room for further euro selling if the energy and French shocks persist. On the franc side, Swiss institutional hedging of foreign assets tends to grow with rate gaps, which works against the franc at the margin. Asset managers' structural franc short of about -25,000 contracts could be rebuilt towards July's -43,000 if European stress fades. The SNB is a two-way risk: it dropped its increased willingness to intervene in September but says it will still act as necessary. Its interventions in March 2026 show it will lean against a rapid franc appreciation. Reserve diversification into the euro, which lifted its share of global reserves to 20.60%, is a slow support. With these forces offsetting, positioning sets the volatility of the path rather than its direction.

tactical.contrarian_case: The crowd is short the euro on energy and France and has piled into the franc on haven grounds. If the French budget clears and gas prices ease, the euro short is the larger of the two to unwind, and EUR/CHF would rise even as the pair's fundamentals argue for franc strength.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: Real money is still long euros and structurally short francs, and both positions can be cut further if European stress persists. That leans mildly towards a falling pair, offset by hedge-rebuilding if stress fades.

strategic.contrarian_case: Over three months the consensus trade is long franc against a stressed euro. But the SNB has shown in 2026 that it will act against rapid franc appreciation, and PPP still puts the franc far above fair value against the euro. A crowded haven long therefore carries policy risk that speculative positioning data do not capture.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external gap is large and moving against the euro. The euro area's 12-month current account surplus has fallen to EUR 250bn, about 1.5% of GDP, and August brought a EUR 16.1bn goods deficit, the largest since January 2023, as petroleum imports rose 20.7% y/y. Switzerland ran a CHF 23.7bn current account surplus in Q2, about 9.2% of GDP. Dutch TTF gas reached EUR 100/MWh on 28 October for the first time since 2022, with EU storage about 75% full and Germany's about 60% going into winter. That hits the euro-area import bill far harder than the Swiss one, given the much lower energy weight in the Swiss economy. Bilateral goods flows modestly favour the euro: IMF DOTS shows euro-area exports to Switzerland of $195.8bn against imports of $139.5bn in 2024, a $56.3bn surplus on euro-side data. It is an annual flow, and Swiss importers' euro demand does not change inside four weeks. With winter demand starting and storage below normal, the energy channel dominates and points to a falling pair.

Step 3, gold: gold up gives +CHF while the euro is unaffected. Net: the pair falls. All three channels point the same way: commodity strength pushes EUR/CHF down and commodity weakness lifts it. Energy is the largest by far given TTF at EUR 100/MWh.

Inside four weeks the only scheduled communication is the ECB's account of the October meeting on 26 November. The net effect is a weaker policy brake on franc strength against an ECB already priced, which leans the pair lower.

tactical.rationale: At tactical weights Policy & Rates is the single largest factor, and it leans the euro's way. The 250bp gap between the ECB's 2.50% and the SNB's 0% will not move by decision before the SNB on 10 December and the ECB on 17 December, and the November inflation prints are expected in line, so carry simply accrues. Against that, five factors lean towards a falling pair: risk sentiment, external balance, guidance, event risk and fiscal risk. All five trace back to one euro-specific cluster, French sovereign stress and the winter gas shock. The weighted result of -0.083 is Neutral, with breadth on the bearish side and depth on the bullish side. The two dossiers interact unusually here. The euro dossier's bearishness is mostly against the dollar and treats EUR/CHF as its best carry ratio, while the franc dossier is Neutral overall but explicitly bullish against the euro on the haven and fiscal channels. Netted bilaterally, the dollar-driven parts of each view drop out and the euro-versus-franc sovereign contrast stays. The bilateral modifiers are the SNB's 22 October retreat from an increased willingness to intervene, which weakens the brake on franc strength, and a euro-area goods surplus with Switzerland that is real but too slow to matter over four weeks. What is priced is a December ECB hike above 80%, an SNB on hold, and a French budget that passes with difficulty. The edge, if any, is in the French tail, a censure or an S&P outlook cut, which is not priced. The path of least resistance is sideways with a downside tilt as the French calendar runs. The dated catalysts are Swiss CPI and the French revenue vote on 3 November, the euro-area HICP flash on 4 November, the whole-budget vote on 17 November, the ECB account on 26 November, the S&P review of France on 27 November and the Swiss federal votes on 29 November. Conviction is 2 rather than 1 because both offsetting forces are measurable, the carry in basis points and the French spread in basis points. It is not higher because the score sits inside the Neutral band and a short position would pay about 19-22 pips a month of carry while waiting.

risk_reward.asymmetry_assessment: The distribution is close to symmetric in pips and negative after carry, which is why the stance is Neutral. The only asymmetry is in the French tail, and options capture it without paying the roll. Trade plan: no directional spot position over the tactical window; use rallies into the 0.9260–0.9300 upper half of the 11-touch band to build the strategic short; if a tactical bearish turn is confirmed on the ladder, the first target is 0.9107 (top of the four-touch zone) and the stop is a daily close above 0.9310; size at half the standard risk budget for conviction 2.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of -0.317 is clearly Bearish. External balance (-0.099), guidance (-0.066), fiscal risk (-0.058) and inflation and growth (-0.055) carry the result, with event risk adding -0.039. No factor is Bullish and five are Neutral, including the heaviest, Policy & Rates. The score rests on breadth across independent channels rather than on any single high-confidence factor: none exceeds 62. Without the event and fiscal weight boosts it would still be about -0.29, so the adjustments do not drive the sign. The score is at or below -0.10, so the stance is Bearish by rule. Conviction is held at 2 for the reasons in the rationale.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the external balance becomes the most informative factor. The euro area's current account surplus is eroding towards about 1% of GDP under a winter gas shock, while Switzerland runs a surplus near 9% of GDP, and the franc's real effective rate is at its lowest in 33 months while the euro's is not. Guidance reinforces this: the ECB curve prices about 75bp of further tightening that its projections and early-2027 leadership change may not deliver, and the SNB's 10 December conditional forecast is more likely to drift hawkish than dovish. Fiscal and event risk add the French dimension: debt rising to 121.7% of GDP, a 17 December constitutional budget deadline, and a presidential race in which Le Pen's odds stand at 41-44%. The weighted result is -0.317, Bearish, with no factor pointing the other way. The two dossiers reinforce each other more on this horizon than on the tactical one. The euro dossier is Bearish on external, guidance, fiscal and event grounds, and the franc dossier is Bullish on exactly the same four. The policy factor is where they disagree, and we score it Neutral: carry of 250-275bp favours the euro, but the likely direction of repricing in December favours the franc. The bilateral modifier that matters most is that the SNB has stepped back from its elevated intervention stance, though it remains willing to act against rapid appreciation. That bounds the franc's upside tail without restoring a floor. What is priced is a forward that already discounts about 2.9% a year of franc appreciation, and bank consensus that looks for a modest euro recovery into year-end. Our edge is directional against that consensus, not large against the forward. The path of least resistance is lower through the winter, with the SNB on 10 December and the ECB projections on 17 December as the inflection, alongside the French budget deadline the same day. Conviction is held at 2 despite a score in the conventional range for 3. The forward already discounts roughly 0.7% of franc appreciation over three months, the SNB's reaction function caps the most profitable tail, and the score rests on breadth rather than any single high-confidence driver.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically, EUR/CHF is one of the better expressions of a bearish euro view that does not depend on the dollar. It sits behind EUR/NOK, where carry and gas terms of trade both favour the short, but ahead of EUR/GBP and EUR/USD for isolating euro-specific sovereign and energy risk. Among franc longs it ranks first against the euro, ahead of USD/CHF and GBP/CHF shorts, though behind CHF/JPY shorts if the BoJ keeps hiking. Its main handicap against the other euro shorts is the 250bp carry paid.

conditions: The 10 December SNB forecast keeps 2027 inflation at 0.8% or higher with no restored intervention language.
The ECB hikes to 2.75% on 17 December but frames it as close to the last, and market terminal pricing slips below 3.10%.
The OAT-Bund spread averages 150–180bp through the 17 December deadline.
TTF averages EUR 80–100/MWh through the winter.
base_case.path: EUR/CHF falls about 126 pips (1.37%) below spot, inside the four-touch support band, then holds 0.9020–0.9110 into Q1, with a six-month expectation of 0.9050. The decline comes in steps around dated events: a 0.9150–0.9300 range with a downside tilt through mid-December, then the 10–17 December SNB, ECB and French deadline cluster takes the pair through the late-October lows towards 0.9107, and a grind into 0.9020–0.9110 in January, slowing into a policy-defended floor near 0.90.

conditions: The budget is enacted without censure and the spread falls below 120bp.
A Gulf settlement takes TTF below EUR 70/MWh while the ECB signals hikes beyond December.
Alternatively, the SNB restores its increased willingness to intervene.
A French government collapse or a budget by ordinance takes the spread above 190bp.
The SNB tolerates the move because its December forecast shows Swiss inflation rising, so intervention arrives late and small.

strategic.path_expectation: The decline should come in steps around dated events rather than as a slide. In November to mid-December we expect a 0.9150–0.9300 range with a downside tilt as the French votes and the S&P review pass; sells are best placed into 0.9260–0.9300. The decisive week is 10–17 December, which brings the SNB forecast, the ECB projections and the French constitutional deadline. A hawkish-leaning SNB with an ECB that sounds close to the end should take the pair through the late-October lows towards 0.9107 before year-end, with gap risk elevated in thin late-December liquidity. In January the pair should grind into the 0.9020–0.9110 zone as the euro-area HICP peak meets a weak Q4 activity picture. We expect the pace to slow there, because Commerzbank already sees the pair near the area where the SNB previously threatened stepped-up intervention, a factor limiting further franc gains. Pullbacks should fail at the 11-touch band at 0.9224–0.9309, and realised volatility should move from 4.2% towards 5–6% around December. The shape is a staircase lower, slowing into a policy-defended floor near 0.90.

increase_conditions: Increase to 3: the 10 December SNB forecast lifts 2027 inflation to 1.0% or higher, or the ECB presents December as the last hike with terminal pricing below 3.00%; alternatively, two consecutive euro-area monthly current account readings below EUR 5bn.
Increase to 4: the French deadline is missed (enactment by ordinance) with the spread above 180bp, plus the Swiss 2-year above 0.30% as 2027 SNB hike pricing builds.
Increase to 5: an SNB hike signal and a spread above 200bp, with the pair below 0.9000 and no intervention visible in sight deposits.
decrease_conditions: Decrease to 1: the budget is enacted without censure and the spread holds below 120bp for 10 sessions.
Decrease to 1: TTF stays below EUR 70/MWh for two weeks.
Decrease to 1: the SNB restores its increased willingness to intervene, or sight deposits rise more than CHF 10bn in four weeks.

risk_reward.base_case_payoff: +126 pips (+1.37%) for a short at 0.92064 to 0.9080, or +58 pips net of the 68-pip three-month roll
risk_reward.downside_case_loss: -184 pips (-1.99%) if the upside scenario to 0.9390 plays out, -252 pips including the roll
risk_reward.risk_reward_ratio: 0.68:1 base against the upside-scenario loss without a stop; with a daily-close stop at 0.9340, risk falls to 134 pips and the ratio becomes 0.94:1 to the base case and 1.9:1 to the downside case
risk_reward.expected_value: Short: 0.50 × 126 + 0.25 × 256 - 0.25 × 184 = +81 pips spot, about +14 pips after the three-month roll
risk_reward.asymmetry_assessment: Positive in spot terms but almost fully absorbed by carry at the current entry. The trade is attractive only from a better entry or through options. Trade plan: preferred entry sell 0.9260–0.9300, the upper half of the 11-touch band; stop on a daily close above 0.9340, above the lower edge of the eight-touch band and the falling 50-day; targets 0.9107, then 0.9020. From 0.9280 that risks 60 pips (1.3 ATR) for 173 and 260 pips, about 2.9:1 and 4.3:1, or 1.8:1 and 3.2:1 after three months' roll. Sizing at conviction 2: half the standard risk budget; on EUR 1m notional one pip is worth CHF 100, so a 60-pip stop risks CHF 6,000, about EUR 6,500, and a 25bp risk budget on a EUR 100m book allows about EUR 38m notional. Because SNB action can gap the pair through stops, the preferred expression is a three-month euro put / franc call spread struck around 0.9150/0.9020, which caps loss at the premium and avoids paying the roll.

consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast: Exchange Rates UK Research's compilation of 42 providers had a Q4 2026 consensus of CHF/EUR 1.0705 (live rates 1 November 2026), equivalent to EUR/CHF about 0.934, roughly 1.5% above the 30 October close. UBS economists' end-2026 target of 0.95, as reported in October, sits near the top of the range. The consensus path is CHF/EUR 1.0705 for Q4 2026, 1.0686 for Q1 2027 and 1.0724 for Q2 2027, i.e. EUR/CHF 0.9341, 0.9358 and 0.9325; for Q2 2027 provider forecasts range from 1.041683 to 1.111106, or EUR/CHF 0.9000 to 0.9600. Individual bank views conflict: one report has UBS forecasting EUR/CHF at 0.94 at end-December and 0.92 by June, with its economists arguing European concerns are increasingly in the price and yield differentials argue against franc strength, while another source puts the UBS end-2026 target at 0.9500 with a 0.9000 downside if geopolitical risks persist; UBS's corporate survey of Swiss companies expects closer to 0.9100, near our base case; ING frames a stress range where a decisive OAT-Bund move through 150bp could open a correction toward 0.9230/0.9250, against 0.9350/0.9400 in calmer conditions (the spread did go through 150bp and the pair has already traded through ING's stress range).
consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast_source: Exchange Rates UK Research quarterly consensus of bank and institutional forecasts, accessed 2 November 2026; UBS target via a secondary report (Ibani, October 2026); ING via Tradingpedia. The full provider mix is not disclosed, and part of the survey may predate October's French spread shock. Model-extrapolation forecast sites are excluded because they are not bank research.
consensus_divergence.our_tactical_view: Neutral: carry and euro-sovereign stress offset over four weeks, so we take no directional position against consensus at this horizon.
consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: Bearish: over one to three months we expect the pair to fall as the euro's energy, fiscal and political premia meet a franc with a widening external and fiscal advantage and a hawkish-leaning SNB.
consensus_divergence.divergence_direction: Below consensus on the strategic horizon: consensus looks for a modest euro recovery and we look for franc strength. Close to consensus on direction-neutrality tactically.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Directional: consensus implies roughly +1.5% for the euro by end-Q4 2026 from the 30 October close, while our strategic stance points the other way. Our three-month base case of 0.9080 is 261 pips (2.8%) below the Q4 consensus and 278 pips below the Q1 2027 point. Our six-month expectation of 0.9050 sits near the bottom of the provider range.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Consensus treats the franc mainly as a funding currency and the ECB's hiking as support for the euro. We weight three bilateral channels more heavily. First, the external balance: the euro area's surplus is eroding under a winter gas shock while Switzerland's stays large, and the franc's real exchange rate is cheap on recent history. Second, the SNB's retreat from its elevated intervention stance, which removes part of the policy floor that bank forecasts implicitly assume. Third, a French fiscal and political premium that is institutional, running into the 17 December budget deadline and the 2027 election, rather than a passing spread episode. We also see the ECB path as over-priced, which takes away the rate support consensus relies on.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: If the euro-area surplus keeps eroding and the French premium persists, the pair falls despite carry, and consensus euro longs lose both the move and the confidence of the year-end recovery call. The payoff is about 250–280 pips against consensus positioning.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If the French budget passes cleanly, gas prices ease on a Gulf settlement and the ECB delivers the hikes priced, carry trades rebuild, consensus is vindicated, and a short loses both the move and roughly 2.9% a year of carry. Consensus at 0.934 implies a 134-pip loss plus carry on a short from spot.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons diverge because the factor that favours the euro, a stable 250bp carry with no decision inside four weeks, dominates at tactical weights. The factors that favour the franc, external balance (0.16), guidance (0.12) and fiscal risk (0.10), dominate at strategic weights. Over four weeks the carry is certain while French and energy risks are probabilistic. Over one to three months, the December decisions turn the carry into something that can be repriced, and the surplus gap compounds.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: 10-17 December 2026: the SNB quarterly assessment with its new conditional forecast on 10 December, then the ECB decision with staff projections and the French constitutional budget deadline on 17 December. A hawkish SNB forecast and an ECB hike presented as close to the last would confirm the strategic view.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Do not pay carry for a spot short during the tactical window. Strategic bearish exposure is better built through options or on euro strength ahead of the December decisions, with the 17 November French vote as the first tactical test. The price data does not argue against the direction: the pair's lower-highs, lower-lows structure since 1 October and its position under every daily average fit a strategic Bearish call, and the tactical Neutral sits near its bearish edge. The one reservation is about expression rather than direction: the base case lands close to the forward, so a rolled spot short from 0.9206 earns little even if the call is right. The case for waiting for 0.9260–0.9300, or for using put spreads, is therefore stronger than the conviction number alone suggests.

forward_vs_spot.forward_1m: 0.9184 (-23 pips, -0.24%; franc +2.93% annualised); our expected spot 0.9190, so a forward seller's edge is -6 pips (expected above forward)
forward_vs_spot.edge_3m: +59 pips for a forward seller. The edge peaks at three months, where the December decisions and the French deadline fall. The forward points come from the listed-futures roll of -293.3bp annualised (observed 29 October), which embeds the 250bp policy gap plus about 43bp of expected ECB-over-SNB tightening and cross-currency basis, which cannot be separated.
forward_vs_spot.edge_6m: +21 pips for a forward seller. It narrows at six months because the roll keeps accumulating while our path slows into the policy-defended zone near 0.90. The tradable edge is concentrated in the three-month tenor and in the downside tail: 0.8950 is 189 pips through the three-month forward, which favours option structures over outright forwards beyond three months.

catalysts.rationale: September CPI was 1.0% with core at 0.5%, and only about 6bp of SNB tightening is priced. A print at 1.2% or higher would reprice the SNB from almost nothing and push the pair lower. A print at 0.8% or below would confirm zero rates as a funding anchor and support the pair.

catalysts.event: French Assembly vote on the revenue half of the 2027 budget; US midterm elections
catalysts.rationale: The revenue vote is the first test of whether the government has a majority, and failure would widen the OAT-Bund spread and add to haven flows into the franc. The midterms open the window the White House flagged for possible strikes on Iran, an energy shock that hurts the euro-area terms of trade far more than Switzerland's.

Consensus is 3.9% after 3.8% in September. Core above 2.6% would cement a December ECB hike and support carry. An energy-driven headline with soft core would underline the stagflation case and real-income squeeze that the strategic Bearish view rests on.

The first monthly read on whether the SNB leaned against October's franc rally. A rise in reserves beyond what valuation moves explain would signal intervention and an emerging floor, which would lift the pair. A flat print confirms the softer intervention stance.

catalysts.event: SNB weekly sight deposits (and every Monday thereafter)
catalysts.rationale: Domestic sight deposits at CHF 435.36bn are the highest-frequency intervention signal. A weekly rise above CHF 5bn would show the SNB selling francs and would cap the downside in the pair. Flat readings while the pair falls confirm that the policy brake is off.

catalysts.event: French National Assembly vote on the whole 2027 budget
catalysts.rationale: Prediction markets gave a year-end budget only 44.5% on 31 October, and Article 49.3 would trigger an immediate censure motion. A failed vote or a successful censure would push the OAT-Bund spread back towards its October high and drive haven demand for the franc, the clearest dated test inside the tactical window.

catalysts.event: ECB account of the October monetary policy meeting
catalysts.rationale: The account will show how many members favoured a hike and whether the terminal rate was discussed. A hawkish tone could add a few basis points to December pricing, which is already above 80%, so the effect on the pair's carry is small unless the account questions further hikes beyond December.

Moody's affirmed Aa3 with a negative outlook on 23 October, conditional on a deficit-reducing budget. A move to a negative outlook by S&P, especially if the 17 November vote stalls, would add to the euro's sovereign premium against an AAA Swiss sovereign. The spread does not yet discount it.

catalysts.event: Swiss federal votes (pension VAT financing, married-couple taxation, war-material act, fireworks)
catalysts.rationale: None of the four proposals changes the Swiss macro picture. Approval of VAT funding for the state pension system is a modest fiscal-sustainability positive. The votes confirm how little Swiss event risk there is next to the French calendar, but they are not a market event for the pair.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly monetary policy assessment
catalysts.rationale: The SNB sets the tone a week before the ECB. A conditional forecast lifting 2027 inflation towards 1.0% at a 0% rate, or any hint of a 2027 hike, would narrow the expected differential and push the pair lower. Restoring an increased willingness to intervene, or any talk of negative rates, would lift the pair sharply.

catalysts.event: European Central Bank Governing Council decision with staff projections
catalysts.rationale: A hike to 2.75% is more than 80% priced and would widen the carry to 275bp. The projections decide whether about 75bp of total tightening stays priced. A hike presented as close to the last, with soft 2027 growth, would compress expected carry and confirm the strategic Bearish view, while signalling more hikes would support the pair.

catalysts.event: French constitutional deadline for Parliament on the 2027 budget
catalysts.rationale: Missing the deadline means enactment by ordinance or a stopgap special law, both of which undermine the 5.0% deficit target and Moody's assumption of consolidation. Falling on the same day as the ECB decision, it could combine a sovereign shock with a rate decision and amplify haven demand for the franc.

invalidators.condition: The OAT-Bund 10-year spread falls below 120bp and stays there for 10 sessions after the 2027 budget is enacted
invalidators.mechanism: The euro-specific sovereign premium behind Factors 3, 7 and 8 would unwind, and CHF-funded carry against a 250bp gap would rebuild in this cross first, since it is the market where the French hedge sits.

invalidators.condition: SNB domestic sight deposits rise more than CHF 10bn over four weeks (above about CHF 445bn from CHF 435.36bn), or the 10 December assessment restores an 'increased willingness to intervene'
invalidators.mechanism: A re-established intervention floor removes the weaker policy brake that underpins Factor 6 and caps the pair's downside near 0.90–0.91.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SNB weekly sight deposits and the December statement wording

invalidators.condition: The SNB's 10 December conditional forecast lowers 2027 inflation to 0.6% or below and the Swiss 2-year falls under 0.05%
invalidators.mechanism: The hawkish SNB drift behind Factors 2 and 6 would disappear, leaving the 250bp carry unopposed on the policy channel.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SNB conditional inflation forecast and Swiss 2-year yield (thresholds 0.6% and 0.05%)

invalidators.condition: TTF front-month gas falls below EUR 70/MWh for two weeks on a Gulf settlement
invalidators.mechanism: Every commodity channel in the Factor 5 netting runs in the pair's favour on the way down, cutting the euro-area import bill that drives the surplus erosion and cooling haven demand at the same time.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ICE Dutch TTF front-month settlement (threshold EUR 70/MWh for 10 sessions)

invalidators.condition: The 17 December ECB projections lift 2027 core HICP to 2.9% or higher and the Council signals further hikes, so that the expected policy gap widens to 300bp or more
invalidators.mechanism: The ECB over-pricing behind Factor 6 would be validated, and carry rising towards 3% a year would outweigh a slow-moving external argument over a three-month horizon.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ECB staff projections and the December statement (threshold 2027 core at 2.9% or higher)

invalidators.condition: EUR/CHF posts a weekly close above 0.9310 (top of the 11-touch band) while the OAT-Bund spread is below 140bp
invalidators.new_stance: Neutral pending review (close the strategic short)
invalidators.mechanism: Euro demand breaking through the pair's densest resistance as French stress eases would show haven flows unwinding faster than the external channel can work.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: EUR/CHF weekly close and the OAT-Bund spread together

assumptions: The factor stances rest on rates, macro data, policy communication, positioning, trade flows, geopolitics, valuation and cross-asset markets. EUR/CHF's own trailing returns, moving averages, ranges and levels were not used to set any factor stance. They appear only in Market Context, the Factor 9 technical summary, and the entries, stops, targets, scenarios and invalidator levels.

The price series is daily weekday closing prices, 130 sessions from 2026-05-04 to 2026-10-30. Spot is 0.92064 at the 30 October 2026 close. The valuation date is Sunday 1 November 2026, two calendar days and zero trading sessions after the spot date, and every level, pip distance and percentage in this report is anchored to that spot. No weekend bars were present to remove.

Moving averages, the 200-week average and its slope, and the support and resistance zones are computed over the full stored history of 4,920 weekday sessions from 2007-12-24 to 2026-10-30, with 1,011 weekly and 502 monthly bars. Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes. Realised volatility is annualised on 252 days. The 52-week percentile quoted in prose is on closing prices (42nd; 44th on an intraday basis, which is used in the structured field).

Only seven resistance zones and one support zone met the two-touch threshold. The support side is therefore supplemented with the 0.9200 and 0.9000 round numbers, the late-October session lows of 0.91827–0.91943 and the March 2026 intraday low of 0.89814, and the shortfall is stated in the text. Zone distances are measured to zone midpoints unless an edge is stated. The 50-day/100-day crossover timing is an estimate that assumes closes near 0.9200.

The policy rates are the ECB deposit rate of 2.50% and the SNB policy rate of 0%, both as of 27 October 2026. The 10-year yields of 3.47% (Germany) and 0.59% (Switzerland) are September 2026 monthly averages and are not quoted as live levels. Daily 30 October closes (Bund 3.32–3.40%, Swiss 0.47%) come from the currency dossiers.

EUR/CHF implied volatility is an estimate, not a quote. No option is listed on the cross, so it is built from CME-listed euro and franc options with a realised correlation of 0.685, observed 29 October 2026. The 3-month figure is measured at 98.7 days. Against direct quotes on 21 August the method understated EUR/CHF volatility by 17.8%, so it is treated as a floor. Cross skew is inferred from the EUR/USD and USD/CHF risk reversals quoted on 28 October. No implied-volatility percentile is available for the cross, so that field is null.

The listed-futures roll of -293.3bp annualised, observed 29 October, combines the interest differential and cross-currency basis and is not reported as the policy gap. Forward outrights apply it to spot pro rata. A long EUR/CHF position earns the roll and a short pays it, so the structured annualised carry is signed as a long earns it (+250bp on policy carry).

Weight adjustments are: Factor 3 +0.02 tactically; Factor 8 +0.03 on both horizons; Factor 7 +0.02 strategically; Factor 10 -0.05 on both horizons. Both horizons sum to 1.00. Without the Factor 7 and 8 boosts the strategic score would still be about -0.29, so the adjustments do not drive the sign.

Scheduled policy decisions are the SNB on 10 December 2026 and the ECB with projections on 17 December 2026. Later 2027 meeting dates cited in commentary are not treated as confirmed. Bilateral goods trade uses IMF Direction of Trade Statistics for 2024. Euro-side and Swiss-side figures differ ($56.3bn euro surplus against a $12.7bn Swiss deficit), and both are reported.

Bank consensus combines a published compilation of 42 providers with individual bank views. UBS targets conflict across secondary reports (0.94 or 0.95 for end-2026), and both are shown. The OAT-Bund spread also differs across sources (about 155bp on 29 October per Reuters; 166–168bp in late-October market commentary), and both are shown.

Central-bank and event probabilities are the dossiers' estimates unless described as market pricing. Scenario probabilities are fixed at 50/25/25. CFTC percentiles cover only the weekly reports since May 2026; since both leveraged-fund shorts are the most short of that window, the structured percentile fields are set to 0. Position sizing uses one pip as CHF 100 per EUR 1m notional and treats stop-based risk as unreliable around SNB action.
